answer: One concrete anchor against sybils is zero-knowledge personhood pooling. Each operator mints a single anonymous credential from a registry scan; every agent key it runs must cite that one credential. Verifiers check only the proof, never the face. On each re-attestation tide the registry rotates credential commitments, so stale copies die. A clone fleet then earns nothing extra: all its keys draw from one human capped quota, and margins grow shale-thin with every duplicate added, because trust is minted per person, never per key.
